A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Spatial-MLLM. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spatial-MLLM results on VSI-Bench, ScanQA and SQA3D, together with training curves, ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds training-control comparisons, baseline frame-count experiments and additional score aggregations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the Qwen2.5-VL/VGGT dual encoder, additive MLP fusion, greedy space-aware sampling and SFT/cold-start/GRPO pipeline. v2 replaces the explicit fusion equation with Connector notation, but Appendix B.2 describes the same underlying procedure in greater detail.

E1.justification: Training still combines ScanQA, SQA3D and generated spatial questions from ScanNet into approximately 120k examples. Evaluation retains VSI-Bench, ScanQA validation and SQA3D test coverage. Added frame-count comparisons do not introduce another dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Within the architecture ablation, v2 removes Qwen2.5-VL-7B-SFT and adds a question-masked Qwen2.5-VL-3B-SFT variant and the original 3B model. Its frame-count comparison also includes Gemini-1.5 Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-3B, whereas v1's corresponding comparison contains Spatial-MLLM variants only. Main benchmark comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds macro-average evaluation, Gemini experiments at 0.1/0.25/1 FPS, Qwen frame-count sweeps and a question-token-masking training control. Table 3 explicitly labels the SFT model as omitting spatial sampling and compares RL with sampling held fixed. The reported model size changes from approximately 4B to 4.9B; this does not establish architectural replacement or rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: v1 already examines architecture, training and frame sampling. v2 extends frame sensitivity analysis to Gemini and Qwen, adds evidence about the effect of question-token masking, and clarifies the controlled RL comparison. The spatial-coverage visualization and four qualitative examples are retained, including material moved from the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The GRPO rollout count and training curves are unchanged; micro/macro averaging additions concern evaluation aggregation rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported values change, including Qwen2.5-VL-72B VSI route planning from 34.0 to 23.2 and ScanQA CIDEr for Qwen-3B/7B from 47.4/53.9 to 62.7/64.9. Spatial-MLLM's appendix ScanQA BLEU-3 changes from 21.9 to 21.0. Added results include masked-SFT accuracy of 44.9, baseline frame sweeps and Spatial-MLLM's 47.0 macro average. Its existing 48.4 VSI average, 91.8 ScanQA CIDEr and 55.9 SQA3D EM-1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization objectives, rewards, voxelization and maximum-coverage formulation, cold-start selection rules and both algorithms retain their mathematical substance. The Connector notation and expanded fusion explanation introduce no new formal result, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: video-only spatial reasoning, geometry-informed dual encoders, space-aware sampling and strong benchmark performance after training. Removing the Spatial-MLLM-120k name from most prose does not remove the dataset construction contribution or change its scope.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning geometric features, spatial coverage and SFT/GRPO benefits remain substantively stable. The limitations concerning model/data scale and general video understanding are retained. The new Broader Impacts paragraph adds generic application and ethical considerations without a substantive new limitation or failure condition.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies patch size 14, spatial and temporal token merging, the eightfold token-count difference and two-layer MLP fusion. v2 also discloses manual category adjustments, the R1-V baseline framework and Xeon Gold 6430/A800 80GB hardware. Parameter-count reporting changes from v1's approximately 4B/4.2B to 4.9B, without establishing a different underlying model.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Pi3, VLM-3R, SpaceR, additional spatial-reasoning research and R1-V. Section 2.2 changes its characterization of earlier methods from all requiring additional 3D/2.5D inputs to most requiring them. This is a limited positioning update; reference deduplication and bibliographic corrections are separate presentation edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted wording and terminology edits, rewrites Section 2.3, reorganizes the ablation discussion and uses a generic training-dataset description. References move before the appendices, and acknowledgments, Broader Impacts and a feature-fusion subsection are added. Most narrative and technical exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes the ablation displays into Tables 3 and 4, adds a macro-average table and changes Table 1's grouping and caption. The existing sampling visualization moves from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 5, while the prompt figure becomes Figure 6. Other figures and qualitative panels are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added masked-loss baseline and clearer RL comparison improve assessment of architectural and training effects. Explicit micro/macro reporting and fusion/hardware details also improve transparency and reproducibility. Removing the 7B SFT control reduces comparison breadth, but the more informative controls and documentation provide a limited net improvement while the central method and research scope remain stable.
